evidence.section: 2.1. Material preparation and hot compression tests
evidence.quote: The experimental temperature was set at 400 ◦C and strain rates were 0.001s – 1, 0.01s-1 and 0.1s-1, respectively, and the sample was 60 %.

Through multiple sampling positions and data analysis, it was found that the N alloy treated at 510 ◦C/16h was mainly in the form of blocky and short rod-shaped LPSO (as indicated by the black arrows in Fig. 1 (a and b)), with a relatively low volume fraction.

After tempering at 510 ◦C/16h + 480 ◦C/8h, the C alloy mainly has dense lamellar LPSO phases distributed within the grains (in the red arrow areas of Fig. 1 (d and e), where the lamellar LPSO phase is the main research object of this paper), significantly increasing the quantity and size of the lamellar LPSO phase.
an intergranular block 18R-LPSO phase is generated

dynamically precipitated a large number of SFs and lamellar LPSO phases in a short time
combined with the dislocations to form stacked faults (SFs)

evidence.section: 3.3. Microstructure evolution of CC alloy and CN alloy after hot compression
